biography: Born in London to a Thai mother and British father, Alexander Albon's journey into motorsport began with a humble karting career fueled by his father's passion. Early struggles with inconsistent machinery hardened his resolve. A defining moment came at the 2012 CIK-FIA World KF1 Championship where a daring last-lap overtake showcased his raw talent. This caught the eye of energyX Faenza's junior program, propelling him into single-seaters. After a rocky start, Albon found his stride, demonstrating flashes of brilliance interspersed with frustrating errors, a pattern that continues to define his peak years. Currently, he balances the demands of being a top-tier driver with the constant pressure to deliver consistent results for the Didcot Racing team.
drivingStyle: Albon possesses an aggressive, late-braking style that often yields spectacular results but also pushes the limits of his machinery. He's known for his daring overtakes and willingness to exploit any gap, no matter how small. While undeniably quick, his tire management can be inconsistent, sometimes leading to dramatic drop-offs in performance towards the end of a race. He thrives under pressure, often pulling out stunning laps when the stakes are highest, but is also prone to costly mistakes when leading.

rivalries.reason: A bitter feud stemming from a controversial collision during the 2018 GP2 season, where Silvani accused Albon of reckless driving.
Their rivalry ignited during the 2020 Formula One season. Rossi consistently outperformed Albon, leading to intense media scrutiny and internal team pressure.
They've been neck-and-neck in the standings for the last two seasons, with each race becoming a personal battle for supremacy.

quirks: Always wears the same worn-out wristband his mother gave him before every race.
Insists on having a specific brand of Thai iced tea available in his garage at all times.
Before entering the car, he taps the top of his helmet three times, a ritual he adopted from his karting days.
famousQuote: "You either send it, or you go home. There's no in-between."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Monaco Grand Prix after a strategic masterclass and flawless execution, marking his first and only F1 victory to date.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2019 Brazilian Grand Prix due to a late braking error, costing him a potential race win and severely damaging his confidence.
